newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower on selling by foreign funds.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower on selling by foreign funds.

text.p: Delhi shares, undercut by political uncertainty, closed modestly lower on Friday on selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs), brokers said.
The Delhi bourse sensitive index shed 2.33 points at 747.69.
"The sentiments of the market will remain depressed as long as political uncertainty persists," said B.K. Nagpaul of brokers B.B. Portfolio.
A senior leader of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition told Reuters on Friday the fate of the 1997/98 (April-March) budget depended on the survival of the government.
Tisco fell 1.45 rupees to 165 on selling by FIIs and profit-taking, brokers said.
ACC lost 21 rupees to 1,383 on selling by FIIs.
State Bank of India dropped two rupees to 272.75.
